message:
fix(host): bind the test hosts to loopback, and stop calling six seconds one

Product 1 (comments), test 2. Two documentation defects and the line that caused the firewall
prompts.

The test hosts never passed --bind-address. It defaults to empty, resolve_bind_address turns that
into INADDR_ANY (host_net_io.cpp:33), and so every listener they opened bound the wildcard. A
wildcard listener on an executable Windows has never seen -- a scratch copy with a new path each
run -- is exactly what raises the firewall prompt, and unanswered prompts became Block rules on
the user's machine. Loopback is all either test ever dials. This is the cause of MY prompts; the
reviewer set the flag and still saw them, so theirs has a different source and their netstat is
what will name it.

The deadline comment said one second and stopped there, which reads as a bound on the call. It is
not. There are three budgets and they add: one second for the wait, five for confirming a kill
(kKillConfirmMs), and about 39ms of spawn and teardown. A call that times out and then meets a
helper that will not die can take about six seconds. That path has never been observed, but the
number to quote for the worst case is six, and the comment now says which one second bounds --
the wait.

And the lingering comment still explained itself by denying the wrong hazard. Replaced with how
the sharing actually works: the helper called OpenFileMapping and MapViewOfFile itself, so it
holds a handle and a view in its own address space, counted separately; UnmapViewOfFile releases
this process's view and the section lives while any process still maps it. There is no page to
fall through. That hazard belongs to threads sharing an address space, which is the thing a
process boundary removes -- and removing it was the point. What holding the handles actually buys
is bookkeeping: an open process handle is one whose exit can still be observed.

Budget 45, wait 20, fetch policy 13, shipped helper gate 16 -- unchanged and passing. The two host
tests still skip by default and were not run.
